Fixture: 09_modular_rgb_64x64_lossless.jxl
64x64 RGB, mathematically lossless, effort 3 -- aims to engage the RCT

Purpose
-------
Targets slices 5/6/7 (modular decoding, frame headers, end-to-end lossless).
Three correlated channels (R ramps along x, G ramps along y, B is a diagonal
sawtooth) give the modular encoder's reversible colour transform (RCT) real
cross-channel structure to exploit -- unlike the single-channel 07/08
fixtures, this one can actually distinguish "decoder applies the inverse RCT
correctly" from "decoder gets lucky because there was only one channel."
-e 3 (above the -e 1 used for 07) gives the encoder enough effort budget to
consider transform selection rather than falling back to the cheapest path.

64x64 is comfortably single-group; it targets transform correctness, not
group/tiling behavior -- see 12_modular_gray_300x200_lossless.jxl for
multi-group coverage.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 3
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_rgb_64x64.ppm  (12301 bytes)
                sha256 8b6d88b2e2da743e0d9638df96f0ec9458d39f4455ccef0f1f33aaa907bf3b65
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted, or consulted. Same formula shape as the
                gradient sources in tools/make-handmade-fixtures.sh, 64x64
                8-bit RGB (PPM P6):
                  R = x * 255 / 63      ramp along x
                  G = y * 255 / 63      ramp along y
                  B = (x + y) mod 256   diagonal sawtooth
                Smooth and cross-correlated between channels, so the RCT has
                real redundancy to remove.

  Fixture:      699 bytes
                sha256 2dcb8438abaa73cb63bdecc3f8221fc3f9866ae97a46f4892fcf7f480a72a355

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run
of tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh). Classified by `jpxl info` (jpxl-cli) as
a recognized "naked codestream".

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
Not independently confirmed which specific transform (RCT vs. something
else) was chosen -- cjxl printed "Modular, lossless" at encode time and
nothing more specific. jxlinfo is not built in this checkout; djxl -v / -v -v
print no per-feature detail for this stream. The fixture is *designed* to
give the RCT something to find (see Purpose above); whether the encoder
actually reached for it is not independently verifiable with the tools
available here. See 07_modular_gray_8x8_lossless.jxl.txt for the general
caveat.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
